items.prompt: The RBAC table lists Contracts as Denied for CLIENT_HR. A CLIENT_HR user sends PATCH /contracts/:id/status to move their own tenant's DRAFT contract to IN_REVIEW. What happens?
items.answer: It succeeds, as that route carries no @Roles list at all
distractors: 403 from RolesGuard, as CLIENT_HR is missing from the list
403 from the controller, as HR may only read contracts
400, as only CLIENT_ADMIN may submit a draft for review
items.explanation: updateStatus has no @Roles decorator, and RolesGuard returns true when no roles are required. The controller only restricts WORKER, and DRAFT to IN_REVIEW is a valid transition, so the code allows what the table says is denied.

items.prompt: A CLIENT_ADMIN sets a worker to ACTIVE while the onboarding plan is still IN_PROGRESS, sending overrideReason "start date moved up". What does the API do?
items.answer: It activates the worker and audits the given reason
distractors: 400, as only internal ops are allowed to supply an override
403, as RolesGuard blocks CLIENT_ADMIN from status changes
400, as the reason must reference an approved document
items.explanation: workersService.updateStatus blocks ACTIVE only when onboarding is incomplete AND no overrideReason is given; it never checks who supplied the reason. The route allows CLIENT_ADMIN, so the documented "internal ops override" is not enforced.

items.prompt: A CLIENT_ADMIN of tenant A calls GET /workers?tenantId=<tenant B id>. What does TenantGuard do?
items.answer: Throws 403, as the requested tenant differs from the token's
distractors: Ignores the query value and just filters by tenant A as usual
Binds tenant B, so the list shows tenant B's workers
Returns 404, so the other tenant's existence stays hidden
items.explanation: For client and worker roles the guard binds user.tenantId, then compares any tenantId in params, query, body or x-tenant-id header and throws ForbiddenException on a mismatch.

items.prompt: A CLIENT_ADMIN of tenant A requests GET /contracts/<id of a tenant B contract>. Which response comes back?
items.answer: 403 saying the contract belongs to another tenant
distractors: 404, as the lookup is filtered by tenant A first
200, as contract ids are globally unique values
401, as the token is only valid for tenant A
items.explanation: findOne loads the contract by id alone, then compares contract.tenantId with the caller's and throws ForbiddenException. A 403 (not 404) confirms that the id exists elsewhere.

items.prompt: A WORKER sends PATCH /contracts/<their own contract>/status with status SIGNED while the contract is still DRAFT. What happens?
items.answer: 400: the service rejects DRAFT to SIGNED as a bad transition
distractors: 403: the controller refuses because the contract is not yet SENT
200: workers may sign their own contract in any of its states
403: workers are blocked from the status route entirely
items.explanation: The controller checks only that the contract is the worker's and that the target is SIGNED. The service then consults validTransitions, where DRAFT allows only IN_REVIEW, and throws BadRequestException.

items.prompt: A client admin wants to move a SENT contract back to DRAFT to fix a typo. What does updateStatus do?
items.answer: It refuses with 400, as SENT can only move to SIGNED
distractors: It allows it, as any non-terminal state may return to DRAFT
It allows it, but writes an audit entry for the rollback
It refuses with 403, as only internal ops may roll back
items.explanation: validTransitions lists SENT: [SIGNED]. Going back to DRAFT is allowed only from IN_REVIEW and APPROVED.

items.prompt: A WORKER posts a comment on their own ticket with isInternal: true in the body. How is the comment stored?
items.answer: As a normal comment, with isInternal forced to false
distractors: As an internal comment, hidden from the worker
It is rejected with 403 for using the flag
As internal, but still visible to the worker who posted it
items.explanation: addComment keeps input.isInternal only for PLATFORM_ADMIN and INTERNAL_OPS; for every other role it stores false, so the comment is visible to client roles.

items.prompt: A ticket has three comments, one flagged isInternal. A CLIENT_ADMIN of the same tenant opens the ticket. How many comments do they see?
items.answer: Two, as internal ones are filtered out for client roles
distractors: Three, because the tenant admins can see the full thread
One, because client admins see only their own comments
Three, but the internal one has its body text redacted
items.explanation: findOne filters out comments with isInternal unless the role is PLATFORM_ADMIN or INTERNAL_OPS, so a client admin gets the two public comments.

items.prompt: A WORKER sends PATCH /workers/<their own id> with a new jobTitle and startDate. What happens?
items.answer: Both fields change; the route has no field limits
distractors: 403: workers may only change their phone number
400: the zod pipe rejects a jobTitle sent by a worker
Only startDate is ignored; jobTitle is updated
items.explanation: The update route checks only that a worker edits their own id, accepts input: any with no validation pipe, and the service writes jobTitle and startDate. Learning task 5 asks you to add the missing 403.

items.prompt: A PLATFORM_ADMIN POSTs a contract with tenantId A in the JSON body and x-tenant-id B in the header. Under which tenant is the contract created?
items.answer: Tenant A: the controller reads the body before the header
distractors: Tenant B: TenantGuard binds the header value first
Neither: TenantGuard refuses the mismatched pair with a 403
Both: one contract is created for each tenant named
items.explanation: TenantGuard binds the header for cross-tenant roles but never rejects a mismatch for them. The create handler then picks req.body.tenantId || req.headers["x-tenant-id"], so the body wins.

items.prompt: A CLIENT_HR user calls GET /contracts. The RBAC table says Denied. What does the code return?
items.answer: 200 with every contract of the user's own tenant
distractors: 403, because CLIENT_HR is not on the route's role list
200 with only the contracts this user has drafted
403, because only workers and admins can read them
items.explanation: findAll has no @Roles decorator and blocks only WORKER; for a client role it filters by req.tenantId and returns the tenant's contracts.

items.prompt: RolesGuard has a special case for one role. Which statement about it is true?
items.answer: PLATFORM_ADMIN passes any @Roles list; INTERNAL_OPS must be listed
distractors: INTERNAL_OPS and PLATFORM_ADMIN both pass any @Roles list
PLATFORM_ADMIN must still be listed on each @Roles route
Any cross-tenant role passes, because TenantGuard set the flag
items.explanation: canActivate returns true for PLATFORM_ADMIN before comparing roles. INTERNAL_OPS is treated like any other role, so it is allowed only where a route lists it (most do). isCrossTenant is not consulted.

items.front: Name the three guards on most controllers and what each one does.
items.back: JwtAuthGuard verifies the Bearer token and puts its payload on request.user (401 otherwise). TenantGuard binds request.tenantId from the token for client roles and rejects any mismatching tenantId in params, query, body or header; PLATFORM_ADMIN and INTERNAL_OPS are marked isCrossTenant and may pick a tenant. RolesGuard checks @Roles metadata, with PLATFORM_ADMIN always passing and routes without @Roles open to every role.

items.front: Give two places where this repo's RBAC table and its code disagree.
items.back: Contracts: the table says Denied for CLIENT_HR, but GET /contracts and PATCH /contracts/:id/status have no @Roles, so HR can list and transition contracts. Onboarding override: the docs say only internal ops may override, but any role allowed on the status route (CLIENT_ADMIN too) can pass an overrideReason.

items.front: What is the contract status matrix?
items.back: DRAFT to IN_REVIEW; IN_REVIEW to APPROVED or back to DRAFT; APPROVED to SENT or back to DRAFT; SENT to SIGNED; SIGNED to ACTIVE; ACTIVE to TERMINATED; TERMINATED is terminal. Workers may only request SIGNED, on their own contract.

items.front: Is the JWT payload in this app encrypted?
items.back: No. A standard JWT is signed, not encrypted: anyone can base64-decode the payload, and the signature only proves it was not altered. The guard verifies the signature and attaches the payload as request.user; never put secrets in it.
